subject: Defining 'Use' — treatment of outputs, retraining, and feedback license
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@brightco.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on MSA: output ownership & training use - BrightCo position

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for sending over the MSA and order form redlines. Our GC asked us to get clarity on three items that are blocking internal approval:

1) Output ownership: BrightCo needs confirmation that outputs generated from our prompts will be owned by BrightCo (including derivative works) and that Redwood will not assert ownership or reuse those outputs.
2) Training/use of customer content: We need an explicit prohibition on using BrightCo content (including prompts, outputs, and metadata) to improve or retrain Redwood models unless we opt in via a separate agreement.
3) Feedback license: If Redwood requires telemetry/feedback for service improvement, we need to see a narrow license that excludes identifiable customer data and includes deletion/retention timelines.

Can you put proposed contractual language against each ask? Also please confirm whether you can provide a short, written example of how you would treat a sample transcript for model improvement (what would be stored, what would be aggregated/anonymized, and what would be retained).

Thanks — happy to set a quick call if it's easier.

Best,
Julia Park
Senior Counsel, BrightCo

Attachment: customer_data_map.xlsx (spreadsheet: high-level map of where data types live)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on MSA: output ownership & training use - BrightCo position

Julia —

Appreciate the clear list. I pulled together an initial draft that maps each ask to a proposed clause and a couple of commercial tradeoffs. High level answers before the draft:

- Output ownership: We typically grant customers ownership (or at least an exclusive license) to outputs for their internal product use, but we need to reserve a narrow, non-customer-identifiable feedback license to maintain/operate the service.
- Training/use: Redwood is generally open to an opt-out for training; if a customer requires a full opt-out, we need to scope increased fees and limitations on features (e.g., no model improvements, slower access to new model versions).
- Feedback license: We can offer a limited feedback license scoped to aggregate/derivative telemetry; we will not use PII or customer-provided protected data to train models if you opt-out.

Attached is a short redline with three alternative output clauses (Customer Ownership / Exclusive License / Limited Service License) and a suggested feedback-license paragraph. See the doc: redwood-output-training-clause-draft.docx.

Proposed next steps: 1) Review the attached text with your GC, 2) tell us which option for output ownership you prefer, and 3) we can propose commercial adjustments. If helpful, we can also produce the sample transcript transformation you asked for.

Short call windows: Friday 10/23 09:30–10:30 PT or Monday 10/26 14:00–15:00 PT.

— Mateo

Date: 2026-10-22T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on MSA: output ownership & training use - BrightCo position

Julia / Mateo —

From a commercial perspective: BrightCo's request for exclusive output ownership is understandable for customer-facing features, but granting exclusivity across the board is not feasible without pricing and operational guardrails. Practical compromise we often take:

- Customer gets full ownership of outputs they incorporate into their product (including derivatives they create).
- Redwood retains the right to use anonymized usage signals/feedback for service improvements under a limited feedback license.
- If BrightCo requires a full training opt-out (no use at all, even aggregated), that is permissible but would move the account to a "no-training" pricing tier with a multi-year commitment.

If you can tell us which of the three output clauses in Mateo's doc you'd prefer, we can run numbers and draft the order form pricing.

— Vanessa
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Julia Park <julia.park@brightco.com>
Date: 2026-10-23T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on MSA: output ownership & training use - BrightCo position

Folks —

I reviewed Mateo's draft and sketched a legal-friendly redline. Key points and suggested language below; I attached a plain-text excerpt as rishi_redline.txt for ease of paste into your doc:

1) Output ownership: Offer a clause where Customer owns Outputs, but Redwood retains a narrow, non-exclusive right to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service stability and security purposes. Suggested text: "Customer retains ownership of Outputs generated solely from Customer Inputs. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may, subject to its Data Protection obligations, use aggregated and de-identified usage data for service improvement and security. Redwood will not use Customer Inputs, Outputs, or other Identifiable Customer Data to train or improve its models without Customer's prior written consent."

2) Training/Model Improvement: If BrightCo requires a strict prohibition on any model improvement uses, we need to capture the operational consequences: no access to alpha features, delayed bug fixes that depend on training signals, and higher per-unit fees. Suggested appendix: "Training Opt-Out — Operational Impact."

3) Feedback license: Define "Feedback" and limit retention: Redwood's Feedback License should be non-exclusive, worldwide, and cover processing for service operations. Include a 90-day retention baseline for raw telemetry and a 2-year maximum for derived aggregate statistics (subject to negotiation). We should also offer deletion windows and show how to submit deletion requests.

4) Auditability & Controls: Offer SOC 2 report references, an export of logs for redaction, and an optional KMS-based separation for customers with strict segmentation needs.

Next steps: Mateo/Vanessa — pick one of the three output options in the draft and I will convert my notes into redlines in the MSA and a short appendix for the order form.

— Rishi
Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: rishi_redline.txt

Thanks Rishi — helpful framing. A few follow-ups from our side after reviewing the proposed text:

- The example language you provided on de-identification is high level. We need a concrete example of the transformation pipeline: where we can expect PII to be removed, what fields you consider "Identifiable Customer Data," and how you validate de-identification.
- Retention windows: BrightCo's minimum requirement is 30 days for raw logs and 12 months for derived products, but we could be flexible if there is a strong rationale for aggregation windows (e.g., security analytics require longer).
- Deletion process: We need a documented API or a contractual SLA for deletion requests and a certification that data has been deleted from backups within a specific timeframe.

We would like to see your proposed MSA redline incorporating Rishi's language and a short appendix that maps the sample transcript to the categories you've described (raw, aggregated, derived), as well as the practical deletion timeline.

If possible, please upload the redline to the Drive folder you referenced and let's pick Monday 10/26 10:00 PT for a deeper discussion with our engineering contact (Marco).

— Julia
Senior Counsel, BrightCo
